paragraphs: Caution signal | This page corresponds to O*NET-SOC 17-1012.00 "Landscape Architects". The official scope is: planning and designing land and outdoor spaces for projects such as parks and other recreational facilities, airports, highways, hospitals, schools, land subdivisions, and commercial, industrial, and residential sites. Typical tasks include communicating requirements with clients and engineering parties, surveying and analyzing site data such as topography and drainage, developing site plans and planting and materials schemes, preparing specifications and cost estimates, and checking during construction whether the site conforms to the drawings. The core deliverable is well-founded, reviewable design documents and implementation check records, not "drawing a nice-looking picture". Risks come from licensed practice and seal authority, professional ethics, the accuracy of site data and drainage analysis, the environment and public safety, and the documentation of design changes and contractor communication. The U.S. figures use the BLS OOH new-period framing (2025 employment 23,500; 2025—2035 growth 4%, average annual openings about 1,700; the May 2025 median annual wage 79,870 USD; main industry professional, scientific, and technical services). For the China wage evidence boundary, see the China salary section. If you find it hard to bear multi-disciplinary coordination, repeated client changes, and schedule pressure, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Ownership of judgment | Real fit comes from whether you can accomplish three things within the same job: make the design real (check the site and client requirements, analyze topography, drainage, and existing conditions, develop site plans and planting and materials schemes, prepare specifications and cost estimates, and produce reviewable design documents); keep licensing and ethics under control (practice within the licensed scope, seal within authorized limits, follow professional ethics and conflict-of-interest rules, comply with codes and public health, safety, and welfare requirements, and act according to the laws and licensing board rules of each jurisdiction); and bear a definable position responsibility (be responsible for the basis of your own designs and documents, and refer matters beyond your practice scope or requiring another professional's signature through the proper process). It is recommended that you test this with a verifiable experience (using public base maps and a fictional site to complete a conditions analysis, two sketch schemes, and a self-check list), rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

Judging suitability | Use the fixed Z site of 200, T / U and the two lines, recompute A6400 exceeding 400 and crossing T, and B5800 leaving 200 but crossing U, which is pending verification; revise the "constructible" draft; see the path for the four works and the seven-day plan of 20—30 minutes per day. Use only paper-based fictional materials, and make no real code judgment, drainage compliance finding, or construction seal.

Fit signal | The work activities of O*NET 17-1012.00 center on thinking creatively and solving problems, getting information, communicating with external people and teams, and analyzing data. If you are willing to compare spatial schemes under site constraints, check topography and drainage data, turn client feedback into drawing revisions, and track implementation quality, these daily demands are closer to your way of working; interest and personality tools are used only for designing exercises and cannot judge licensing qualifications or performance.

Landscape Architect corresponds to the U.S. O*NET-SOC 17-1012.00 "Landscape Architects". The official scope is: planning and designing land and outdoor spaces for projects such as parks and other recreational facilities, airports, highways, hospitals, schools, land subdivisions, and commercial, industrial, and residential sites. The typical work loop is communicating requirements, surveying and analyzing topography and drainage, developing site plans and planting and materials schemes, preparing specifications and cost estimates, and then checking whether construction conforms to the drawings. The U.S. figures on this page use the BLS OOH new-period employment and the BLS OEWS wages presented by O*NET (2025 employment 23,500; 2025—2035 growth 4%, average annual openings about 1,700; the May 2025 median annual wage 79,870 USD, 10th percentile 54,770 USD, 90th percentile 130,190 USD, median hourly 38.40 USD; main industry professional, scientific, and technical services); for the China wage evidence boundary, see the China salary section. This page does not constitute legal or practice advice.

entries: Objects of work | The objects are the site and existing conditions, client and project requirements, codes and public health and safety requirements, planting and materials, and interfaces with other disciplines such as engineering and architecture, with design and design management carried out within licensing and ethical boundaries.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable conditions analysis and site assessment, site plans and scheme comparison drawings, planting and materials lists, specifications and cost estimates, construction check and change records; the results must be traceable to site data, code bases, and client confirmation.

Complete workflow | Communicate requirements → survey and analyze site data such as topography and drainage → develop site plans and planting and materials schemes → prepare specifications and cost estimates → check during construction and handle changes.

paragraphs: Key judgments | The O*NET work context shows: email 100% every day, indoors environmentally controlled 85% every day, telephone conversations 65% every day, face-to-face discussions 53% every day, work with a group or team 63% extremely important, time pressure 60% at least once a week but not every day, exactness or accuracy 50% very important, decision freedom 50% some freedom. The basis for judgment is site and existing-conditions data, code and public safety requirements, and the boundaries of licensed scope and professional ethics. For the environment and rhythm see also: Environment and rhythm | The work alternates mainly between office design and on-site checking: sitting 55% more than half the time, work week 65% more than 40 hours, written letters and memos 50% at least once a week but not every day, contact with others most of the time 40%, coordinating or leading others 37% very important, dealing with external customers 40% very important, task priorities and goals 40% some freedom. The rhythm is driven by bids, approvals, and construction milestones. These are U.S. respondent distributions, not uniform working hours or rhythm for every position in China.

Environment and rhythm | The work alternates mainly between office design and on-site checking: sitting 55% more than half the time, work week 65% more than 40 hours, written letters and memos 50% more than once a week, contact with others most of the time 40%, coordinating or leading others 37% very important, dealing with external customers 40% very important, task priorities and goals 40% some freedom. Research inputs | The official RIA is retained, and detail R74/I62/A61/C45/E44/S28 is interest intensity and does not rebuild codes; Job Zone4 is general preparation and is not marked Bright Outlook. In 2025 the industries were professional, scientific, and technical services 51% and administrative support 20%; the remaining 29% is only the difference and does not establish a government share. In 2025 the U.S. annual wages at the 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles were 54,770, 64,170, 79,870, 104,090, and 130,190 USD; the official hourly wages were 26.33, 30.85, 38.40, 50.04, and 62.59 USD. The new BLS period runs from 2025 employment of 23,500 to 24,500 in 2035, growth 4%, net gain 1,000; average annual openings about 1,700 including growth and replacements. O*NET is currently also on 2025—2035; the shared old-period register and the protected FAQ retain historical values.

The first things this job checks are: the objects (site and existing conditions, client and project requirements, codes and public safety requirements), the inputs (measured and public site data, planning and design codes, existing utility and ownership information, contract and licensing requirements), and the deliverables (conditions analysis, site plans and scheme comparison, planting and materials lists, specifications and cost estimates, construction check records). Anything unverified should be treated as pending verification, and experience or intuition cannot replace site data and code bases.

To judge the work loop, look at four steps: input check (confirm site data, codes, and licensed scope) → task definition (design within the licensed and contractual scope, without exceeding authority to seal or taking on another discipline's responsibility) → execute and record (complete the analysis, schemes, documents, and construction check traces) → review and escalate (stop immediately and co-sign or refer when data or codes are in doubt, or when another discipline or a conflict of interest is involved). The loop holds only if the site, codes, and documents are verifiable, not merely if the drawings are finished.

Adjacent duty boundaries | This page covers only the precise O*NET-SOC 17-1012.00 occupation "Landscape Architects". Adjacent occupations such as architects (except landscape and naval), architects, agricultural engineers, and architectural and civil drafters differ in work objects, licensed scope, and responsibility boundaries, and cannot be swapped based only on job titles, nor can proxy framings replace jurisdictional licensing, seal authority, and professional ethics requirements. This page does not constitute legal or practice advice.

Architects (except landscape and naval) direction | The core output is building and interior space design with structural and MEP coordination. This occupation focuses on land and outdoor space, landscape elements, and site drainage; the objects and licensing systems differ, and titles alone cannot be swapped.

Architects direction | The core output is the overall design of individual buildings and building groups. This occupation deals with the relationship between the site and outdoor space; the design objects and the division of responsibility for structures and fire safety differ, and licensed scope must be checked separately.

Agricultural engineers direction | The core output is engineering schemes for agricultural production systems, irrigation, and soil and water. This occupation focuses on site design and public space; the engineering calculations and licensing responsibility differ, and the two cannot be applied to each other.

Architectural and civil drafters direction | The core output is drafting and revising drawings according to the design intent. This occupation bears scheme and design responsibility and may seal according to license; drafting and design responsibility are at different levels and must be checked separately.
The work objects of a landscape architect and the AI boundary: which steps may be assisted and which judgments must remain with people.

Generative AI can trial approved fictional record summaries, scheme text, or list drafts; mentions of conventional CAD/GIS design software differ from generative AI adoption. Check back against the original site, codes, and versions, and do not claim efficiency gains without measurement. Supported tasks under supervision and independent practice are separate, and licensing and sealing follow jurisdictional rules; the model confers no authority, and final professional responsibility cannot rest on outputs alone.

Evidence note | ILO2025 global task exposure and the NIST general risk framework do not measure adoption rates, efficiency, or layoff dates for this occupation; ASLA/CLARB are used for member ethics and jurisdictional licensing and do not support AI effects. In 2025 the only U.S. job posting showed AutoCAD44%, SketchUpPro39%, Photoshop22%, CreativeCloud19%, Office17%, InDesign16%, Civil3D12%, Excel / Revit / Illustrator each 11%, PowerPoint9%, ArcGIS6%, Outlook5%, Word / MicroStation each 3%, Project <1%; Acrobat / Access showed no percentage, which is not equal to 0. A mention is not generative AI adoption or a position requirement.

Difference note | You may use Z to compare the time and errors of manual work and tool-based checking of 200, 6400 / 5800, the T / U conflict, and the erroneous draft; the text being checkable is only a test design condition, and no acceleration is claimed without measurement.

Chain of responsibility | From confirming site data and authorization, through tool processing, human review, and finalizing the design and documents, to construction checking and changes, every step must be clear about who is responsible, and traceable evidence must be retained; design documents and seals must not rely on model outputs alone.

Tool use | First do Z manually, then use approved tools to draft the list or the pending-verification note and check it back against the prompt; do not treat software mentioned in postings as a measured generative AI efficiency gain, and key professional judgments and statutory sealing are still checked under responsibility and licensing.

May be assisted: organizing site and code materials, generating sketch schemes and alternatives, first drafts of planting and materials lists, document proofreading, and compliance check prompts; the results of these steps can be checked afterwards, but the site data, the code text, and the design intent must still be revisited.

Human control points | Check the original site, codes, versions, and other-discipline interfaces, and distinguish supported work under supervision from independent practice; statutorily required licensing and sealing must be compliant, and ASLA members sign according to the rules only when they have direct professional knowledge or supervisory control.

Occupation comparison | The U.S. 17-1012.00 on this page is only compared on tasks with landscape design positions in China, and this round established no precise national wage mapping; NBS industry or broad occupational group averages cannot replace a national occupational median or percentile.

China scope | Chinese enterprise design qualifications, individual professional titles, employer hiring, and specific document responsibility are each checked separately. The Fuzhou landscaping center reply concerns the professional titles of personnel for enterprise design qualifications and explains the Fujian review scope, and cannot be generalized into a uniform national individual license or mapped onto U.S. licensure. The Beijing Institute of Architectural Design 2026 campus recruitment announcement was published on 2025-09-29: it includes landscape design, requires a bachelor's degree or above in a related field for 2026 graduates, and sets general requirements for code compliance, software, and collaboration; the online application window 2025-09-24—10-24 has closed. It lists no landscape headcount or salary and does not prove current hiring or a national threshold. One line of the text mentions 2024 campus recruitment, which is inconsistent with the title's target window; the explicit 2026 cohort and the 2025 application dates are used instead, without guessing the reason.

Insufficient evidence: this round established no Chinese national occupational wage percentile or starting pay precisely corresponding to U.S. 17-1012.00. The National Bureau of Statistics 2025 tables are industry and broad occupational group pretax annual averages and exclude the self-employed and freelancers; industry averages, U.S. percentiles, and a single posting cannot fill the gap. The Beijing Institute of Architectural Design sample lists no landscape salary, and restricted access does not mean China has no wage statistics.

AI and wages | This round established no causal data on generative AI adoption, efficiency, and wages for this occupation; no pay increase is predicted from software mentions or exposure, nor is it claimed that pay necessarily stays unchanged.
U.S. salary reference | Taken from BLS OOH and the BLS OEWS presented by O*NET (May 2025), under the precise 17-1012.00 occupation framing.

Direct answer | In 2025 the U.S. annual wages at the 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles were 54,770, 64,170, 79,870, 104,090, and 130,190 USD; the official hourly wages were 26.33, 30.85, 38.40, 50.04, and 62.59 USD. In 2025 the industries were professional, scientific, and technical services 51% and administrative support 20%; the remaining 29% is only the difference and does not establish a government share. The distribution is not an industry wage.

OEWS covers employer wages and includes incentive pay, excludes overtime pay, non-production bonuses, and employer-paid benefits, and excludes the self-employed; percentiles are not starting pay, after-tax pay, or a personal quote, and official hourly wages are disclosed separately.

Interpretation note | This framing can be used to understand the wage distribution and demand direction for this occupation, but not as a personal quote, and it cannot be compared directly with mainland China or any other market; licensing, employer type, and project type affect actual income, and statistical percentiles do not correspond to a specific position.

Industry framing | In 2025 the industries were professional, scientific, and technical services 51% and administrative support 20%; the remaining 29% is only the difference and does not establish a government share. BLS2025 employment by industry was architectural, engineering, and related services 50%, landscape services 20%, self-employed 17%, government 8%, and construction 1%, which are finer industries plus the self-employed classification. In 2025 the industry median annual wages were government 107410, architectural, engineering, and related services 82290, construction 71990, and landscape services 65150 USD, and these cannot be applied to the 51/20 broad categories or to self-employed income.

Influencing factors | Employer type (design firm, engineering company, government department, or self-employment), region, project type, and whether one holds a license and seniority affect actual income level and stability; the percentiles on this page are statistical positions and do not correspond to a specific institution or position.

For a landscape architect, which interests, abilities, and work styles matter more? This page discusses fit only through work samples and responsibility boundaries, and does not use personality labels to replace licensing qualifications or performance judgment.

Direct answer | The fit signal is a willingness to compare spatial schemes under site constraints, check topography and drainage data, turn client feedback into drawing revisions, and track implementation quality, while complying with the licensed scope and professional ethics, rather than a personality label. Interest and personality tools can only help design exercises and cannot judge licensing qualifications or performance.

Positive signals | Can form scheme comparisons on site and code bases and explain the trade-offs; can make design documents into reviewable drawings, specifications, and lists; can check and record changes during construction.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include insufficient site data or drainage judgment bases, schemes conflicting with codes or public safety requirements, failure to identify existing utilities or ownership constraints, exceeding the licensed scope or failing to handle conflicts of interest ethically, and changes without documentation; if you find it hard to bear multi-disciplinary coordination, repeated client changes, and schedule pressure, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Paper exercise | Recompute Z 200, A6400 exceeding 400 and crossing T, and B5800 leaving 200 but crossing U, write a conditions matrix, and revise "constructible"; the path has a fixed prompt, a reference deliverable, four works, and a seven-day plan. The works do not prove on-site code compliance, personality performance, or licensing.

Conclusion | The activity preference is closer to a combination of Realistic, Investigative, and Artistic (the O*NET interest code RIA, including the nature and outdoors direction); but an interest code can only help design exercises and cannot judge licensing qualifications or performance.

Personality boundaries | This round established no predictive validity of scales for landscape architect performance; use the Z conditions matrix, cost recomputation, and draft revision to raise specific questions, and do not derive licensing, performance, or hiring from personality labels.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks can only help raise questions and cannot replace this occupation's licensing qualifications, professional ethics, and actual design performance evidence; no tool conclusion constitutes a licensing, sealing, or hiring judgment.

Licensed practice and sealing risk | Trigger: issuing documents, sealing, or taking design responsibility in a jurisdiction or professional field where one is not licensed or beyond the licensed scope. Consequence: may violate practice law and endanger public health, safety, and welfare. Control: check the jurisdictional license and professional scope, seal within the authorized scope, and co-sign or refer when necessary. Boundary: licensing and seal authority are determined by the laws and licensing board rules of each jurisdiction.

Professional ethics risk | Undisclosed interests, improper gifts, or misrepresentation may trigger member discipline and trust risk. The ASLA code applies to members; the consequences of complaints differ between should ethical standards and shall rules of conduct. R1.203 interests must be disclosed, and not all conflicts must be avoided; R1.108 multiple-party fees require the written consent of all parties. Specific situations such as government-related business or a public reviewer's own financial or family interests are avoided according to the rules; improper influence through contract gifts and false statements of qualification are prohibited. State law and contracts are checked separately.

Site and environmental data risk | Trigger: topography, drainage, soil, or existing utility and ownership information not verified. Consequence: may cause design defects, ponding, or construction disputes. Control: check measured and public data, request supplementary surveys when necessary, mark uncertainties, and co-sign. Boundary: survey and other professional conclusions are issued by the corresponding responsible parties.

Public safety and code application risk | Trigger: incorrect code application, or grading and drainage design not meeting safety requirements. Consequence: may cause personal and property risk. Control: check the applicable codes and standards, conduct a safety review of the scheme, and keep calculation and basis records. Boundary: code application is governed by the current rules of the jurisdiction.

Change and contractor communication risk | Trigger: changes during construction not documented, or oral instructions replacing written documents. Consequence: may cause cost and responsibility disputes. Control: changes are governed by written documents and confirmation records, check whether the site conforms to the drawings, and keep correspondence records. Boundary: change approval and contractual responsibility are determined by the contract and the employer's rules.

Preparation and licensure | All 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia license landscape architects. Typical education includes an accredited bachelor's or master's degree in landscape architecture, and some jurisdictions allow alternative paths; education, supervised experience, and examination conditions are set separately by the target jurisdiction, and most allow sitting the exam while accumulating experience. Passing the four parts of the LARE satisfies the examination requirements of member jurisdictions and does not automatically confer a license or seal authority. Job Zone4 is a general description of occupational preparation and cannot replace licensing law.

Entry check | First check the specific education, experience, examination, and licensing conditions of the target jurisdiction; do not uniformly treat a bachelor's degree as the only path or assume the exam must come after finishing an internship. The Beijing Institute of Architectural Design 2026 campus recruitment announcement was published on 2025-09-29: it includes landscape design, requires a bachelor's degree or above in a related field for 2026 graduates, and sets general requirements for code compliance, software, and collaboration; the online application window 2025-09-24—10-24 has closed. One line of the text mentions 2024 campus recruitment, which is inconsistent with the title's target window; the explicit 2026 cohort and the 2025 application dates are used instead, without guessing the reason.

Typical education includes an accredited bachelor's or master's degree in landscape architecture, and some jurisdictions allow alternative paths; education, supervised experience, and examination conditions are set separately by the target jurisdiction, and most allow sitting the exam while accumulating experience. Passing the four parts of the LARE satisfies the examination requirements of member jurisdictions and does not automatically confer a license or seal authority. Job Zone4 is a general description of occupational preparation and cannot replace licensing law. The Fuzhou landscaping center reply concerns the professional titles of personnel for enterprise design qualifications and explains the Fujian review scope, and cannot be generalized into a uniform national individual license or mapped onto U.S. licensure.

Qualification boundaries | Education, supervised experience, examination, licensing, employer hiring, and specific sealing are different states; ASLA member rules also require direct professional knowledge or supervisory control, and no one signs work without a basis.

Paper exercise Z | Entirely fictional, and not to be used for field measurement, construction, or code compliance findings. The simulated site runs from southwest (0,0) to northeast (20,10), area 200 simulated m²; the retained tree zone T is x=8—10, y=4—6, and the utility pending-verification zone U is x=14—16, y=7—9. Scheme A has 80 hardscape and 120 planting, with a circulation line (0,5)→(20,5); scheme B has 60 hardscape and 140 planting, with a circulation polyline (0,5)→(0,8)→(20,8)→(20,5). Simulated unit prices are 50 for hardscape and 20 for planting in budget units per m², with a budget of 6000; excludes survey and maintenance. The given rules: Z1 the circulation line may not cross T; Z2 crossing U must be pending verification and must not be marked constructible; Z3 the two area types totaling 200 and a list ≤6000 only means the simulated budget is met. Task: draw the two lines and T / U, recompute the area and cost of both schemes, list violations and pending items, and write the reason for continuing the comparison; the erroneous draft "B is cheaper and already approved, constructible" must be corrected. Without elevation, soil, actual utility, and drainage data, do not design real slopes, drainage, or safety codes.

Reference deliverable | A area 80+120=200, cost 80×50+120×20=6400, over budget by 400; the y=5 horizontal line crosses T and does not satisfy Z1/Z3. B area 60+140=200, cost 60×50+140×20=5800, remaining 200; the y=8 horizontal line avoids T but crosses U, Z1/Z3 is satisfied, and Z2 utilities are still pending verification. You may continue comparing B and request utility and other materials, but cannot judge either scheme constructible; the unknown must not be treated as nonexistent. Correct the draft to "B satisfies only the given area and simulated budget; utilities and the real site/codes are pending verification, and no construction documents have been issued". Four works: a conditions/constraints and schematic drawing marking T / U and the two lines, a cost list for both schemes, a matrix of satisfied/violated/pending conditions, and the unissued version with the reason for choice and the information request. The paper areas do not prove the real layout, plant suitability, or drainage safety, and do not confer sealing qualification.

Seven-day plan | 20—30 minutes per day: day 1 draw the 200 site and T / U; day 2 draw the A / B circulation lines; day 3 check 200 and 6400 / 5800; day 4 check A crossing T, B crossing U, and the pending items; day 5 correct "already approved and constructible" and list the information requests; day 6 ask a peer to cross-check only the four paper works and keep versions; day 7 assemble the deliverable, and separately check the target jurisdiction's degree/experience/examination/licensing and the specific employer's requirements. No field construction, drainage testing, or automatic qualification conclusion.

Transfer paths | Site analysis, scheme representation, documents, and cross-disciplinary coordination can be compared; architecture and agricultural engineering require separate checks of design calculations and licensing, and the drafting direction requires additional technical drafting, version control, and materials engineering knowledge, so independent design sealing must not be treated as a uniform entry point for drafting.

Transferable abilities | The shared foundations across adjacent directions include: site and data analysis, scheme comparison and representation, code and document preparation, cross-disciplinary coordination, and construction checking and records; but each path must fill in the evidence corresponding to its new duties and licensing requirements.

Transfer boundaries | The two frozen targets in architecture, comparison and special topic, do not construct different U.S. SOC codes; agricultural engineering requires systems engineering calculations and specific qualifications, and drafting requires detailed drawings, versions, materials, and engineering knowledge, and does not confer independent design sealing. The last two architecture special items are the same as the earlier target and are not six independent occupations.

entries.answer: Paper exercise Z | Entirely fictional, and not to be used for field measurement, construction, or code compliance findings. The simulated site runs from southwest (0,0) to northeast (20,10), area 200 simulated m²; the retained tree zone T is x=8—10, y=4—6, and the utility pending-verification zone U is x=14—16, y=7—9. Scheme A has 80 hardscape and 120 planting, with a circulation line (0,5)→(20,5); scheme B has 60 hardscape and 140 planting, with a circulation polyline (0,5)→(0,8)→(20,8)→(20,5). Simulated unit prices are 50 for hardscape and 20 for planting in budget units per m², with a budget of 6000; excludes survey and maintenance. The given rules: Z1 the circulation line may not cross T; Z2 crossing U must be pending verification and must not be marked constructible; Z3 the two area types totaling 200 and a list ≤6000 only means the simulated budget is met. Task: draw the two lines and T / U, recompute the area and cost of both schemes, list violations and pending items, and write the reason for continuing the comparison; the erroneous draft "B is cheaper and already approved, constructible" must be corrected. Without elevation, soil, actual utility, and drainage data, do not design real slopes, drainage, or safety codes. Reference deliverable | A area 80+120=200, cost 80×50+120×20=6400, over budget by 400; the y=5 horizontal line crosses T and does not satisfy Z1/Z3. B area 60+140=200, cost 60×50+140×20=5800, remaining 200; the y=8 horizontal line avoids T but crosses U, Z1/Z3 is satisfied, and Z2 utilities are still pending verification. You may continue comparing B and request utility and other materials, but cannot judge either scheme constructible; the unknown must not be treated as nonexistent. Correct the draft to "B satisfies only the given area and simulated budget; utilities and the real site/codes are pending verification, and no construction documents have been issued". Four works: a conditions/constraints and schematic drawing marking T / U and the two lines, a cost list for both schemes, a matrix of satisfied/violated/pending conditions, and the unissued version with the reason for choice and the information request. The paper areas do not prove the real layout, plant suitability, or drainage safety, and do not confer sealing qualification. Seven-day plan | 20—30 minutes per day: day 1 draw the 200 site and T / U; day 2 draw the A / B circulation lines; day 3 check 200 and 6400 / 5800; day 4 check A crossing T, B crossing U, and the pending items; day 5 correct "already approved and constructible" and list the information requests; day 6 ask a peer to cross-check only the four paper works and keep versions; day 7 assemble the deliverable, and separately check the target jurisdiction's degree/experience/examination/licensing and the specific employer's requirements. No field construction, drainage testing, or automatic qualification conclusion.

source_card.note: Source note | Official RIA/JobZone4 / not marked Bright, the 2025 five wage percentiles and the official hourly wages are retained; BLS and O*NET are both currently on 2025—2035, the industry distribution was updated in 2025, and broad-industry and fine-industry wages are kept separate. The old-period register cited by the protected FAQ is not synchronized. ASLA member ethics, U.S. jurisdictional licensing, and Chinese enterprise qualification titles are not interchangeable; CLARB covers bachelor's and master's degrees and jurisdictional alternative paths, and passing the examination is not a license. The NBS official broad-industry pretax annual average already lists two proxy references, which are not national landscape occupational wages; the Beijing Institute of Architectural Design historical application has closed, and headcount and salary are not listed. ILO/NIST are general research and risk material, and CAD software in postings is not a generative AI effect. Z is entirely fictional, with 200 and 6400 / 5800, the T / U conditions, and the unissued-version four works over seven days; it does not serve as construction compliance or qualification proof. The NIST shared judicial wording is protected by the FAQ, and this round keeps the registration and records the conflict.
